hook.situation: A normal day in Korea can bring four short messages: a delivery driver asks where to leave a package, a pharmacist asks about symptoms, your building posts an inspection notice, and the subway announces a delay. You do not need to produce a long answer, but you do need to understand what happened and what action is expected.
objectives: Read common delivery requests and confirmations without translating word by word.
Recognize the questions and dosage instructions used at clinics and pharmacies.
Find the time, restriction, and required action in housing and transit notices.
hook.whyItMatters: These messages are short, but missing one ending can change the required action. This chapter trains you to identify status, request, restriction, and next step in the notices you actually meet while living in Korea.

grammarNotes.title: V-아/어 주세요 / V-(으)면 연락 주세요 — delivery requests and updates
grammarNotes.func: Delivery messages usually contain one concrete request and one condition. V-아/어 주세요 asks someone to do an action, while V-(으)면 marks the condition that triggers the next action: 도착하면 연락 주세요 means 'Please contact me when you arrive.' Look for the action closest to 주세요 to find what the sender wants.

formTable.when: A direct but polite delivery request
formTable.ex: 놓다 → 문 앞에 놓아 주세요 (Please leave it at the door.)

formTable.when: A condition followed by a request
formTable.ex: 도착하다 → 도착하면 연락 주세요 (Please contact me when you arrive.)

formTable.when: A more careful request to the driver
formTable.ex: 보내다 → 사진을 보내 주실 수 있을까요?

examples.en: Please leave it at the door.
examples.note: 문 앞 is the location; 놓아 주세요 is the requested action. 놓아 is often shortened to 놔 in casual messages.

examples.en: When you arrive, please text instead of calling.
examples.note: -지 말고 replaces one action with another: not a call, but a text.

examples.en: Your parcel has been left with the security office.
examples.note: 맡겨 두었습니다 reports that the parcel was placed there and remains available for pickup.

examples.ko: 배송 완료 사진을 보내 주실 수 있을까요?
examples.romanization: baesong wallyo sajineul bonae jusil su isseulkkayo?
examples.en: Could you send me a delivery-completion photo?
examples.note: -주실 수 있을까요? is useful when asking a driver for an extra action without sounding demanding.

keyPoint.label: Find location, trigger, and requested action
keyPoint.body: In 문 앞에 놓아 주세요, the location is 문 앞 and the action is 놓다. In 도착하면 문자 주세요, the trigger is 도착하면 and the requested action is 문자 주세요. Reading these parts separately lets you understand the message even when particles are omitted.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 놓아 주세요 is carefully [노아 주세요] and is often contracted to 놔 주세요 [놔 주세요] in speech. 맡겨 is pronounced [맏껴], with the following ㄱ becoming tense.

drill.instruction: Read the message and identify the required action.
drill.model: 도착하면 문자 주세요. → Action: send a text after arrival.
items: 문 앞에 놓아 주세요. → Where should the parcel go?
전화하지 말고 문자 주세요. → Which action should be avoided?
경비실에 맡겨 두었습니다. → Where is the parcel now?

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 도착하면 연락해요. = a clear request to the driver
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 도착하면 연락 주세요. / 도착하면 연락해 주세요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: A plain -해요 sentence can sound like a statement about what normally happens. In a delivery instruction, 주세요 or 해 주세요 makes the requested action explicit.

grammarNotes.title: N도 있으세요? / V-(으)세요 — clinic questions and medicine instructions
grammarNotes.func: At a clinic or pharmacy, staff often ask whether an additional symptom is present with N도 있으세요? and ask about your condition with 어디가 불편하세요? Instructions usually end in -(으)세요: 식후에 드세요 means 'Take it after meals.' The ending is polite, but the message may be a question, an instruction, or a recommendation depending on intonation and context.

formTable.when: Asking whether another symptom is present
formTable.ex: 열도 있으세요? (Do you also have a fever?)

formTable.when: Asking which body part feels wrong

formTable.ex: 먹다 → 식후에 드세요 (Take it after meals.)
하루에 세 번 드세요 (Take it three times a day.)

examples.en: Besides the cough, do you also have a fever?
examples.note: 말고 means 'apart from / instead of.' 도 asks about an additional symptom.

examples.en: Where are you feeling the most discomfort?
examples.note: 불편하다 can cover pain, irritation, and general discomfort, so it is broader than 아프다.

examples.ko: 이 약은 하루에 세 번 식후에 드세요.
examples.romanization: i yageun harue se beon sikhue deuseyo.
examples.en: Take this medicine three times a day after meals.
examples.note: Read the frequency and timing separately: 하루에 세 번 + 식후에.

examples.en: It may make you drowsy, so do not drive.
examples.note: The first clause gives a possible side effect; -지 마세요 gives the restriction.

keyPoint.label: Separate symptom, frequency, timing, and warning
keyPoint.body: A medicine message can contain four different facts: what symptom it treats, how often to take it, when to take it, and what to avoid. In 하루에 세 번 식후에 드세요, 세 번 is frequency and 식후에 is timing. Never treat the whole line as one memorized block.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 식후 is pronounced [시쿠] because ㄱ and ㅎ combine into ㅋ. 드세요 is [드세요]; it is the honorific everyday form used instead of 먹으세요 for medicine and food.

drill.instruction: Extract the practical information from each clinic or pharmacy line.
drill.model: 하루에 두 번 드세요. → Frequency: twice a day.
items: 식후 30분에 드세요. → When should it be taken?
열도 있으세요? → What additional symptom is being checked?
운전하지 마세요. → What must the patient avoid?

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 열이 나요 is the only possible way to mention a fever.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 열이 나요. (reporting the symptom) / 열도 있으세요? (checking its presence)
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: 나다 is the most useful pairing when you report that a fever developed. 있다 is also natural when a medical worker checks whether the fever is present. The surrounding task changes the preferred verb.

grammarNotes.title: V-아/어야 해요 / V-지 마세요 — housing notices and building rules
grammarNotes.func: Apartment and management-office notices tell you what is required, prohibited, or temporarily unavailable. V-아/어야 해요 marks an obligation, V-지 마세요 marks a prohibition, and N 중 marks an activity currently in progress. First find the date and time, then find the action ending.

formTable.when: A facility is being checked or repaired

examples.ko: 내일 오전 10시부터 두 시간 동안 단수예요.
examples.romanization: naeil ojeon yeol sibuteo du sigan dongan dansuyeyo.
examples.en: The water will be shut off for two hours starting at 10 a.m. tomorrow.
examples.note: 부터 gives the start; 두 시간 동안 gives the duration; 단수 gives the service interruption.

examples.en: Do not use the elevator during the inspection.
examples.note: 중에는 defines the restricted period; -지 마세요 states the prohibited action.

examples.en: Recyclables must be put out on Tuesday evening.
examples.note: The topic is 재활용품; the required time is 화요일 저녁.

examples.en: Please contact the management office about any problems.
examples.note: 관리실로 marks the contact destination; 불편 사항 means an issue or inconvenience to report.

keyPoint.label: Read notices in this order: when → what changes → what you must do
keyPoint.body: 내일 오전 10시부터 / 단수 / 물을 미리 받아 두세요 means: start time / service change / preparation. Korean notices often omit a personal subject, so focus on time words and the final action ending rather than looking for 'you.'

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 단수예요 is pronounced [단수예요]. 점검 is [점검], and 관리실로 links as [괄리실로] in standard pronunciation because ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

drill.instruction: Read each notice and state what the resident must do.
drill.model: 점검 중에는 이용하지 마세요. → Do not use it during inspection.
items: 오전 10시부터 단수예요. → When does the water stop?
물을 미리 받아 두세요. → What preparation is requested?
화요일 저녁에 버려야 해요. → When should it be put out?

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 단수예요 means the building has no water permanently.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 단수예요 means the water supply is temporarily shut off; check the stated start and duration.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Housing notices normally pair 단수 with a time range. Missing 부터, 까지, or 동안 can make you misunderstand a temporary interruption as a permanent condition.

grammarNotes.title: N부터 N까지 / N 동안 — finding time ranges in notices
grammarNotes.func: Notices often place the time before the main event. 부터 marks the starting point, 까지 marks the endpoint, and 동안 marks the duration. First find these time markers, then read what service changes or what action is required.

examples.romanization: ojeon yeol sibuteo ohu han sikkaji dansuyeyo.
examples.en: The water will be shut off from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.
examples.note: The 부터…까지 frame gives the full service-interruption window.

examples.en: The inspection will continue for three hours.
examples.note: 동안 gives the duration, not the finishing clock time.

examples.romanization: oneul ohu yeol sikkaji taekbaereul chajagaseyo.
examples.en: Please pick up the parcel by 10 p.m. today.
examples.note: With one time followed by 까지, the time is usually a deadline.

examples.en: Normal service operates from Monday through Friday.
examples.note: 부터 and 까지 can mark days as well as clock times.

keyPoint.label: Range and duration answer different questions
keyPoint.body: 오전 10시부터 오후 1시까지 answers 'from when until when?' 세 시간 동안 answers 'for how long?' A notice may show both, but either one can be enough to plan what to do.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 부터 is [부터]. 시간 동안 is pronounced as written, [시간 동안], with each word kept clear. 까지 is [까지] with a tense ㄲ.

drill.instruction: Decide whether the highlighted time marks a start, deadline, full range, or duration.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 두 시간까지 점검해요. = The inspection lasts for two hours.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 두 시간 동안 점검해요. = The inspection lasts for two hours.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: 까지 marks an endpoint or limit. To state how long an event continues, use 동안. Use 까지 only when 'up to two hours' or a deadline is the intended meaning.

grammarNotes.title: N이/가 지연되다 / V-는 중이다 — transit delays and transfers
grammarNotes.func: Transit announcements describe current status before giving the next action. 지연되다 means 'be delayed,' 운행이 중단되다 means service has stopped, and 운행 중이다 means service is operating. Transfer instructions use N으로 갈아타세요 and exit instructions use N번 출구로 나가세요.

formTable.when: A train or bus is delayed
An operation is currently in progress

examples.en: Line 2 trains are currently delayed.
examples.note: 현재 marks the current status; 지연되고 있습니다 is a formal announcement style.

examples.en: Transfer to Line 3 at the next station.
examples.note: 에서 marks the transfer location; 으로 marks the new line.

examples.ko: 사고로 인해 일부 구간의 운행이 중단됐습니다.
examples.romanization: sagoro inhae ilbu guganeui unhaengi jungdandwaetseumnida.
examples.en: Service has been suspended on part of the route due to an accident.
examples.note: 일부 구간 means only part of the route, not the entire system.

examples.en: Bus service is expected to resume shortly.
examples.note: 재개되다 means resume; -(으)ㄹ 예정입니다 reports the announced plan.

keyPoint.label: Status first, action second
keyPoint.body: 현재 열차가 지연되고 있습니다 only reports status. 다른 교통편을 이용해 주세요 adds the action expected from passengers. Do not assume every delay announcement means service has stopped; distinguish 지연, 중단, and 재개.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 지연 is [지연]. 갈아타세요 is pronounced [가라타세요] as the final ㄹ of 갈 links to 아. 중단됐습니다 is commonly heard as [중단됟씀니다].

drill.instruction: Classify each announcement as delay, suspension, resumption, or transfer.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 지연되다 and 중단되다 both mean the service has completely stopped.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 지연되다 = be delayed / 중단되다 = be suspended or stopped
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: A delayed train may still arrive and operate. 중단 signals that service is not operating on the stated section. This distinction changes whether you wait or find another route.

exampleSentence.en: Please contact me from the shared building entrance.
Please leave the parcel with the security office.
exampleSentence.note: 맡기다 is used when leaving something in another person's care.
Often paired with a number of minutes.

exampleSentence.en: Check the directions for taking the medicine.
exampleSentence.note: A label word seen on medicine packages.

exampleSentence.en: Contact the management office if there is a problem.
exampleSentence.note: Used in apartments and office buildings.

exampleSentence.ko: 배관 공사로 두 시간 동안 단수예요.
exampleSentence.en: The water will be shut off for two hours due to plumbing work.
exampleSentence.note: Check the time range that follows.

exampleSentence.en: There will be a regular elevator inspection.

exampleSentence.note: Often appears with 운행 or 열차.

exampleSentence.en: Transfer to a bus at this station.
exampleSentence.note: 환승하다 and 갈아타다 express the same practical action.

exampleSentence.en: Service is scheduled to resume in the afternoon.

extendedDialogue.setting: Alex is handling four ordinary messages during one day in Seoul and checks the important details with a Korean friend.

lines.speaker: 택배 기사
lines.en: I'm at the building entrance. Where should I leave it?
lines.grammarNote: -아/어 드릴까요? offers an action for the recipient.

lines.speaker: 알렉스
lines.ko: 문 앞에 놓아 주시고 사진도 보내 주세요.
lines.romanization: mun ape noa jusigo sajindo bonae juseyo.
lines.en: Please leave it at my door and send a photo too.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Besides the cough, do you also have a fever?
lines.grammarNote: 도 asks about an additional symptom.

lines.speaker: 알렉스
lines.en: Yes, I've had a slight fever since last night.
lines.grammarNote: 부터 identifies when the symptom began.

lines.speaker: 친구
lines.ko: 관리실 공지 봤어요? 내일 오전에 단수래요.
lines.romanization: gwallisil gongji bwasseoyo? naeil ojeone dansuraeyo.
lines.en: Did you see the management-office notice? They say the water will be off tomorrow morning.
lines.grammarNote: -래요 reports the notice in casual speech.

lines.speaker: 알렉스
lines.en: Yes, I'm planning to store some water in advance.
lines.grammarNote: -아/어 두다 keeps the prepared result available.

lines.speaker: 안내 방송
lines.ko: 2호선 운행이 지연되고 있으니 다른 교통편을 이용해 주세요.
lines.romanization: ihoseon unhaengi jiyeondoego isseuni dareun gyotongpyeoneul iyonghae juseyo.
lines.en: Line 2 service is delayed, so please use another form of transportation.
lines.grammarNote: The first part gives status; the final part gives the passenger action.

readingText.title: 오늘 받은 생활 안내 네 개
readingText.body:
[배달] 고객님, 문 앞에 택배를 두었습니다. 배송 완료 사진을 확인해 주세요.
[약국] 이 약은 하루에 세 번 식후에 드세요. 졸릴 수 있으니 운전하지 마세요.
[관리실] 내일 오전 10시부터 12시까지 배관 점검으로 단수됩니다. 사용할 물을 미리 받아 두세요.
[교통] 현재 2호선 열차가 지연되고 있습니다. 시청역에서 1호선으로 환승해 주세요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: [Delivery] Your parcel has been left at your door. Please check the delivery-completion photo. [Pharmacy] Take this medicine three times a day after meals. It may make you drowsy, so do not drive. [Management office] The water will be shut off tomorrow from 10 a.m. to noon for plumbing inspection. Store the water you need in advance. [Transit] Line 2 trains are currently delayed. Please transfer to Line 1 at City Hall Station.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 약을 먹은 뒤에 피해야 하는 행동은 무엇인가요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 졸릴 수 있으므로 운전을 피해야 합니다.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 단수는 언제이고 무엇을 준비해야 하나요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 내일 오전 10시부터 12시까지이고, 사용할 물을 미리 받아 두어야 합니다.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 열차가 지연될 때 어느 노선으로 환승해야 하나요?

culturalNote.title: Korean notices often omit 'you'
culturalNote.body: Delivery texts, medicine labels, apartment notices, and transit announcements rarely repeat a personal subject. The time phrase and final ending carry the practical information: 오전 10시부터, -지 마세요, -아/어 주세요, -될 예정입니다. Reading those anchors is faster and safer than searching for a full English-style sentence.
culturalNote.tip: On every notice, mark three things: time, current status, and required action. If one of the three is absent, check whether the message is only an update rather than an instruction.

inlineExercises.prompt: 도착하면 전화하지 말고 문자 주세요. What should you do?
inlineExercises.explanation: -지 말고 rejects the call and replaces it with 문자 주세요.

inlineExercises.prompt: 택배를 경비실에 맡겨 두었습니다. Where is the parcel?
inlineExercises.explanation: 경비실에 gives the current parcel location.

inlineExercises.prompt: 이 약은 식후에 드세요. When should you take it?
Which question checks for an additional fever?
inlineExercises.explanation: 도 adds fever to symptoms already mentioned.

inlineExercises.prompt: 오전 10시부터 두 시간 동안 단수예요. When does it start?
점검 중에는 이용하지 마세요. What does the notice prohibit?
열차가 지연되고 있습니다. What is the status?
inlineExercises.explanation: 지연 means delay, not full suspension.
갈아타다 means transfer to another vehicle or line.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which word means service will start again?
inlineExercises.explanation: 재개 is resumption; 중단 is suspension.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which reading order is most useful for a practical notice?
inlineExercises.explanation: These three anchors reveal what changed and what you must do.

bullets: Delivery: find the location, arrival condition, and action closest to 주세요.
Clinic and pharmacy: separate symptom, frequency, timing, and warning.
Housing notices: read the time range before 단수, 점검 중, -아/어야 해요, or -지 마세요.
Transit: distinguish 지연 (delay), 중단 (suspension), 재개 (resumption), and 환승 (transfer).
Korean notices often omit the subject; time, status, and final ending carry the message.

writingTask.prompt: Read four short notices and write one English action line for each. Do not translate every word; state only what you need to know or do.
writingTask.hint: For each notice, identify time, current status, and requested or prohibited action.
writingTask.model: 문 앞에 두었습니다. → The parcel is at my door; check it. / 식후에 드세요. → Take it after meals.
writingTask.modelEn: This is a reading-comprehension task: reduce each Korean notice to one practical action in English.

canDo: Understand delivery requests and locate a parcel from a driver message
Read symptom questions and medicine frequency, timing, and warnings
Find the time and required action in a building-management notice
Distinguish a transit delay, suspension, resumption, and transfer instruction
